limitations: Schuh uses 120 cycles over 23 days, with 73 cycles at 40 s and the others at 20 s, and approximately 140 minutes per full cycle. Two 4.6 ms magnetron pulses and an intentionally deformed readout potential distinguish this experiment from proton-mass PnA acquisition.

The readout uses C2=-0.5997, C4=-0.00223(18), C6=0.014(4) and a maximal magnetron radius near 274 micrometers. Harmonic potential during phase evolution and deformed potential during readout must not be conflated.

The 43 microhertz statistical error is enlarged by sqrt(2) to 61 microhertz because the reduced chi-square is 2. Tilt fluctuations cannot be separated from voltage fluctuations by the axial signal alone.

The image-charge difference subtracts ideal 390.723(1) mHz, magnetic 0.056(21) mHz and tilt/ellipticity 0.188(37) mHz from 393.258(61)(77) mHz. The resulting 2.291(61)(111) mHz combines correlated correction uncertainties.

The 73 and 37 microhertz tilt contributions are correlated and add to 110 microhertz. The two 21 microhertz magnetic contributions cancel in the stated analysis; quadrature of all marginal errors would misrepresent that covariance.

Appendix A uses the 2017 proton mass and compares an axial calibration ratio over 1000 measurements drawn from both the image-charge and proton campaigns. This shared input prevents a claim of fully independent proton-mass validation.

Dividing the Table I difference by the charge-state difference of five gives 458.2 microhertz, before the small axial contribution, rather than Table II 471.9. review.limit: The actual two-page scan was read and visually inspected only for the Schwinger letter beginning on page 416 and ending on page 417. The neighboring letters on calcium and silver are excluded. The letter is dated 30 December 1947 and was published in 1948. Schwinger's two-page 1948 letter announces a leading perturbative magnetic correction with renormalized experimental mass and a separate discussion of charge renormalization. In its Gaussian-unit convention alpha=e^2/(hbar*c), the displayed correction becomes a_e^(1)=alpha/(2*pi). The historical decimal 0.001162 is not a modern precision prediction; no undocumented alpha input or loop calculation is reconstructed. Atomic-moment and atomic-energy examples mentioned in the letter are not admitted as separately reviewed experiments. The leading anomalous moment is not a statement that all radiative effects are vacuum polarization, that virtual excitations are an observed particle population, or that the vacuum is a material substance. The low-order formula does not reproduce modern higher-order QED, lepton, hadronic or weak contributions, nor does Fan's experimental extraction require the Schwinger term as a calibration input.

records.description: For the source isolated identical spheres in the far-separation Debye-Huckel regime, use U(x)/(kB*T)=Zeff^2*lambdaB*[exp(kappa*a)/(1+kappa*a)]^2*exp(-kappa*x)/x. Here x is center-to-center separation, a is sphere radius, Zeff is effective charge in units of the positive elementary-charge magnitude, kappa is inverse screening length and lambdaB=e^2/(epsilon*kB*T) in the source electrostatic-cgs convention. This is a screened repulsive pair term, with finite-sphere amplitude and an effective charge that need not equal titratable charge.

The selected equation omits van der Waals and hydrodynamic contributions in the declared highly charged, resolved regime. It is not a complete repulsion-plus-attraction DLVO potential, near-contact model, coagulation barrier, aggregation-rate law or stability theorem.

A fitted dilute isolated-pair potential is not automatically an exact pair-additive description of a dense suspension, phase boundary or many-body structure. Walls, charge regulation, ionic contamination and nonlinearity require separate checks.

contexts.finding: For the selected rapidly cooled Al-Mn material, the source reports sharp electron diffraction with six fivefold, ten threefold and fifteen twofold axes of an icosahedral point group, with orientational correlation across finite grains up to about 2 micrometers. Dark-field imaging, small-volume convergent-beam diffraction and powder diffraction support the authors rejection of a conventional multiply twinned Bravais-lattice explanation. The icosahedral phase is metastable under the reported protocols: no detectable subsequent crystallization after 6 hours at 300 degrees C or 1 hour at 350 degrees C, and conversion to stable Al6Mn after 1 hour at 400 degrees C.

limitations: The ILL (SERI) 2.5 mm gamma-diffraction crystals are distinct from WS1 and from the general silicon average. Comparator material is adjacent, not a measurement of the exact illuminated volume of every capture crystal.
The W04 reference is 192.0155702(10)e-12 m; NW04=192.0155696(10)e-12 m is transferred through impurity corrections within the same boule. The two ILL paths share absolute-standard inputs.
Table 4 uses ILL-WS1=40(10)e-9 and WS1-NW04=-20(9)e-9; adding 25e-9 material variability gives ILL 192.0155735(56)e-12 m. Table 5 uses three transfer crystals, giving 192.0155707(59)e-12 m.

The reported final ILL spacing is 192.0155721(64)e-12 m at 22.5 C and zero pressure. The final uncertainty is larger than either path uncertainty; the complete combination rule has not been recovered and independent inverse-variance averaging is not justified.

Repeated-comparison scatter uses a standard deviation, not a standard error of the mean. The added 25e-9 material variability is empirical; Table 16 also contains SRM k=2 entries, which are not interchangeable with the ILL k=1 specimen uncertainty.
